summary: Orchestrate tenant-gated onboarding binding: auto-create Jira project, Confluence space, and Slack channels with conditional retention + Legal/Security approver chain
description:
Request: Build an automated tenant-scoped onboarding gateway that provisions a Jira project, Confluence space (templated), and Slack channels (private + public variants) when a new business tenant/team is approved. The gateway must enforce conditional retention policies on Confluence and Slack (based on data classification), and kick off an approval chain that includes Legal and Security before spaces are created for tenants classified as 'sensitive'.

Background: Product Ops and Platform receive frequent manual requests to create project spaces for new tenant teams. Compliance requires retention baseline and Legal approval for any tenant handling regulated data. The current manual process is slow and error-prone (ticket escalations, missed retention settings). This automation should reduce support load and enforce guardrails consistently.
impact: Manual provisioning requires 2-3 support staff hours per request and leads to inconsistent retention settings and missing approver evidence. Risk of non-compliance for regulated tenants and delayed onboarding affecting sales and CSM SLAs.
current_behavior: Onboarding requests come via a support form → manual triage by Platform-CS → engineer creates Jira project, Confluence space, and Slack channels; manual retention settings are applied if requested. Legal/Security approvals are collected as email threads and attached to tickets.
expected_behavior: Self-serve gateway: Product Ops or solutions engineers can submit a tenant onboarding request form that triggers an automated workflow. Workflow evaluates tenant data classification, routes approval requests to Legal/Security when required, and only after approvals provisions Jira/Confluence/Slack via service accounts with correct permission templates and retention tags. An audit trail (Confluence page and ticket activity) is created automatically.
steps: 1) User fills 'Tenant Onboard' form with tenant name, owner, classification, and required templates
2) Gateway evaluates classification and applies policy rules (sensitive → require Legal & Security approval)
3) Approval tasks are created and routed to on-call Legal/Security approvers; reminders if not responded in 48h
4) Upon approval, gateway provisions Jira project (with permissions groups), Confluence space from template (with retention tags), and Slack channels via provisioning bot
5) Gateway posts a summary to #platform-onboarding and attaches approval artifacts and links to a created Jira issue for traceability
acceptance_criteria: A) Gateway can provision Jira/Confluence/Slack for a new tenant using service accounts with least privilege
B) For 'sensitive' classification, approvals from Legal and Security are required and enforced by the workflow (no provisioning without both approvals)
C) Retention settings are applied to Confluence spaces and Slack channels according to classification and are visible in audit logs
D) Created Jira issue contains links to approvals, Confluence space, and Slack channel; permissions and membership follow template
E) Monitoring: failures emit alerts to #platform-ops and create an incident ticket automatically

investigation_notes: Checked existing automation: INT-997777 contains a provisioning gateway prototype that uses GitHub Actions to call service endpoints — could be reused but lacks approval routing
Confluence templates: templates exist under OPS templates but are not parameterized for retention tags. Need template variables for data_classification and retention_period
Slack provisioning: current bot supports channel creation and invites; retention settings require Enterprise Grid API calls (audit: confirm token scopes)
Permissions: Jira project template must create groups prefixed with tenant_<short>_admin/read and add OKTA group sync mapping; ensure SCIM/Group sync is part of design
Audit trail: store approval artifacts as attachments on the resulting Jira issue and a snapshot page in Confluence; retention of approval artifacts must be immutable for 3 years for regulated tenants
resolution_notes: Design/requirements approved in triage; next steps: author RFC linked to this ticket, assign eng owner for implementation, and schedule Security/Legal integration session. MVP plan: implement provisioning for non-sensitive tenants first (no approvals), then add approval step for sensitive tenants.
next_steps: Create RFC in Confluence and link back to this ticket
Assign eng owner and add to infra backlog
Security/Legal to provide approver rotation roster and SLAs
notes_for_impl: Use existing workflow-engine integration where possible. Reuse INT-997777's provisioning adapters but replace ad-hoc scripts with idempotent API calls. Ensure service account keys are stored in KMS and rotated per policy. Add metrics: time-to-provision, approval latency, failure rate.
